Scan a publication folder for disclosure risks

Source: R/scan-outputs.R
nis_scan_outputs.Rd

Check CSV, TSV, XLSX, HTML, Markdown, text, and DOCX files in a folder and its subfolders. The scan flags known HCUP identifier names and potential unmasked counts of 1 through 10 in recognizable count columns or explicit statements such as "n = 5" and "5 discharges".

Usage

nis_scan_outputs(path, error = FALSE)

Arguments

path

Directory containing the files you intend to publish.

error

If TRUE, stop with class easyNIS_output_scan when any finding is present. The condition carries a findings data frame.

Value

A data frame with file (relative path), location (file, document part, sheet, table or column), issue (restricted_identifier, small_count or scan_error), and field (the recognized identifier name, or NA). A finding can represent several matches in one location. Cell contents and reader diagnostics are omitted.

Details

This check is heuristic. An identifier name can appear in a legitimate methods description. Review unsupported files (including images and PDFs), renamed identifiers, unfamiliar table layouts, and counts recoverable from totals, percentages, or other releases by hand.

XLSX uses readxl. HTML and DOCX use xml2, and Markdown also uses commonmark. A supported file that cannot be read, including when an optional reader is missing, produces a scan_error.

See also

Check disclosure before sharing results

Other disclosure: nis_cell_counts(), nis_suppress()

Examples

folder <- tempfile()
dir.create(folder)
writeLines(c("group,n", "A,3", "B,20"), file.path(folder, "table.csv"))
nis_scan_outputs(folder)
#>        file      location       issue field
#> 1 table.csv file column 2 small_count  <NA>
unlink(folder, recursive = TRUE)
